entries.title: I Samuel 7:1
segments: The ordinances of God will benefit all who rightly observe them, but none who continue to neglect them.

entries.title: I Samuel 7:2
segments: It was twenty years; after the ark was brought to Kirjath-jearim, before the Israelites humbled themselves and turned to the Lord as related in the following verses.

entries.title: I Samuel 7:3
segments: By the right use of means which God has provided, men are bound to prepare their hearts for his service.

entries.title: I Samuel 7:4
segments: Baalim and Ashtaroth; images of Baal and Astarte.

entries.title: I Samuel 7:5
segments: Penitent confession of sin, and humble prayer for divine mercy, are essential to forgiveness, and are a sure preparation for the reception of divine favors.

entries.title: I Samuel 7:6
segments: Poured it out before the Lord; by this symbolical act, in connection with fasting and prayer, they seem to have denoted the entire prostration of their souls before God in humble penitence.

entries.title: I Samuel 7:8
segments: All who have right views of God and of themselves, will place a high value on the prayers of his people, and will earnestly desire them.

entries.title: I Samuel 7:10
segments: Humble, believing, earnest, persevering prayer has great influence with God, and is instrumental of unspeakable good to men.

entries.title: I Samuel 7:12
segments: Eben-ezer; meaning, the stone of help, or the help-stone.

entries.title: I Samuel 7:15
segments: Rulers who are men of prayer, and who transact their civil duties in the fear and love of God, are great blessings to the people.

entries.title: I Samuel 7:16
segments: Bethel was north, and Mizpeh (in the original Mizpah) north-west from Jerusalem.

entries.title: I Samuel 7:17
segments: Rameh; in Benjamin, generally supposed to be the same as Ramathaim-zophim.
